identity.title: JWST/NIRCam Imaging of the Bipolar Planetary Nebula NGC 6537: The (Infra)red Spider, Revealed

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have made use of archival data from HST and the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) as points of comparison with our new JWST/NIRCam near-IR imaging of NGC 6537.

question.value: What is the structure and mass-loss history of the bipolar PN NGC 6537, and is there evidence for a binary central star, from JWST/NIRCam, ALMA, HST and Chandra imaging?

evidence.quote: The resulting multiwavelength view of the Red Spider establishes the detailed lobe/torus structure of the nebula and the mass-loss history of its progenitor star.
This paper makes use of ALMA data ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00424.S.
The ALMA data were obtained in the 3 mm region (ALMA Band 3) as part of a molecular line survey of high-mass star-forming regions (cite: Gieser2023)

method.value: Velocity-integrated (moment 0) images over various velocity ranges and intensity-weighted mean velocity (moment 1) image from the cube

evidence.quote: we have extracted velocity-integrated (“moment 0”) images over various velocity ranges of interest as well as an intensity-weighted mean velocity (“moment 1”) image.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive torus size, velocity and age

method.value: Projected radius ~9 arcsec read from map; deprojected using the lobe-axis inclination; age = radius/velocity

evidence.quote: we deduce a projected angular radius of $\sim$9$''$ for the outer edge of the molecular torus, leading to a deprojected linear radius of $\sim$0.13 pc assuming $D=1.8$ kpc.

assumptions.value: Torus axis inclination equals polar axis inclination (38 deg to plane of sky); D = 1.8 kpc

evidence.quote: if we assume the inclination of the molecular torus axis of symmetry with respect to the plane of the sky is identical that of NGC 6537’s polar axis

used_for.value: Convert Chandra count-rate limits to flux limits (APEC model)

evidence.quote: we used the webPIMMS[^2] spectral modeling tool. We adopt the APEC thermal plasma model
Version 1.14.0 of the JWST Science Calibration Pipeline was used to generate fully calibrated exposures and final mosaiced images
characterized by a projected expansion velocity of $V_{exp} \sim 10$ km s$^{-1}$
the deprojected expansion velocity of the torus we obtain from the $^{13}$CO(1–0) data is $\sim$13 km s$^{-1}$
leading to a deprojected linear radius of $\sim$0.13 pc assuming $D=1.8$ kpc
The implied torus dynamical age — or, more accurately, the time since onset of copious equatorial mass loss — is then $\sim$10000 yr.
$L_{X,d} \lesssim 1.5\times10^{31}$ erg s$^{-1}$

findings_qualitative.value: 13CO traces a point-symmetric equatorial torus whose symmetry axis (PA~155 deg) is rotated ~20 deg from the expected equatorial plane

evidence.quote: the projected orientation of peak $^{13}$CO emission (PA $\sim$155$^\circ$) is evidently rotated by $\sim$20$^\circ$

claims.hypothesis: Is the molecular gas a slowly expanding equatorial torus older than the polar lobes?
claims.experiment: ALMA 13CO(1-0) moment maps compared with JWST imaging
claims.result: Torus ~10 km/s, 0.13 pc, ~10000 yr vs lobes ~3700 yr
claims.finding: Slow equatorial mass loss preceded fast polar outflows

evidence.quote: This timescale is significantly larger than the $\sim$3700 yr dynamical age of the lobes

claims.hypothesis: Does the central star host hot circumstellar dust?
claims.experiment: Aperture photometry on HST and JWST images, blackbody fit
claims.result: IR excess matched by ~1000 K blackbody
claims.finding: Likely circumbinary dust disk implying a binary

evidence.quote: The IR excess can then be well matched by a model blackbody that peaks at a wavelength of roughly 3.5 $\mu$m, corresponding to a blackbody temperature of $\sim$1000 K

limitations_admitted.value: X-ray limits depend on assumed plasma temperatures

evidence.quote: the limits on both $L_{X,d}$ and $L_{X,p}$ derived here are dependent on the aforementioned choices of parameters

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA data analysis is qualitative, with no uncertainties on torus radius or velocity
Distance uncertainty (±0.5 kpc) propagates to ages but is not quantified
Inclination of torus assumed equal to lobes despite the observed misalignment
